text:
ops-bot: P0: GPU pool us-west-2 has reached critical saturation. pending_queue=28,100, throttled=1.7k/s. Autoscaler reports repeated placement failures. Paging @oncall-ml.

pagerduty: paging @oncall-ml for P0 incident (GPU capacity).

oncall-ml: ack. jumping on. what error are we seeing from scheduler/autoscaler?

ops-bot: autoscaler: create_node attempt failed: cloud error "QuotaInFlight" then subsequent attempts returned "PlacementFailure: CapacityFragmentation". Scheduler log snippet: `WARN scheduler: cannot find layout for pod seq-run-9b3 requested=[2xA100-80GB contiguous] available_layouts=[1xA100-80GB, 4xA100-40GB] score=-inf`.

luis: customer reports spiking 429s on text-gen endpoints. Opening INC-4809. Affected: most standard customers + heavy sandbox jobs. Enterprise reserved pools unaffected.

anika: investigation: node inventory shows a drift: recent node pool upgrades flipped some hosts to default-mig-profile=80/80 while older hosts remained 40/40/40. Many of our multi-GPU models request contiguous 80GB slices across two GPUs, so scheduler refuses mixed nodes. Autoscaler keeps adding nodes but they join with mismatched MIG config.

rachel: metrics: total_free_gpu_ram=1.8TiB across pool, but contiguous 80GB-pair capacity = 0. Pending pods requiring 2x80GB = 44. Queue growth rate +3k/min.

sam: immediate mitigations suggested: 1) route non-critical customers to low-memory quantized variant (v2-small-quant) 2) apply emergency per-tenant throttles to batch/long-run jobs 3) add temporary scheduler flag to allow placement on mixed-MIG nodes with guardrails 4) start controlled drain/reprovision of mixed-MIG nodes.

oncall-ml: prefer routing+throttle first to avoid risking OOMs. We can enable scheduler override as last resort. How fast is routing change?

anika: routing change via router-console takes ~3m; I'll prepare change to route non-enterprise -> v2-small-quant for 45m. Also increase cache TTLs for small models.

luis: enabling throttles now: set batch_concurrency_limit for sandbox/standard to 40% of previous. Command: `/infra ratelimit set global.batch_limit 0.4x`. Applying.

ops-bot: router-bot: requested route patch staged. Will rollout in 2m.

infra-bot: autoscaler-note: we observed 6 node create events in last 12m. All became Ready but kubelet label `gpu.mig.profile` shows mixed values on ~17 nodes. Those nodes display free memory but are incompatible with scheduler layout constraints.

rachel: we should also check if our model footprints can be reduced temporarily (split across smaller slices) by using model sharding or lower batch sizes. Any fast shim?

oncall-ml: we can enable per-request model sharding for a handful of non-critical campaigns, but it's intrusive. Instead prefer small-quant fallback. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: router-bot: route change applied. Non-enterprise traffic -> v2-small-quant for 45m. Smoke tests OK.

luis: throttles live. Observability shows queue growth slowed; pending_queue peaked at 28.1k and now flattening near 24k. 429 rate for standard tier dropped from 9% -> 2.2% after 10m.

anika: infra plan: start targeted drains for greatest-mismatch nodes in 12m. We'll cordon + drain 2 nodes at a time with `--max-surge=1`. Recreate with uniform MIG profile=40GB where possible. Estimated time 90-180m to finish whole pool.

sam: recommend we also bump autoscaler cooldown to 8m to avoid oscillation while nodes are being reprovisioned.

oncall-ml: customer comms: pinged CS to send a notice to affected standard tier customers. Also flagged major accounts for potential direct reach-out.

rachel: one-off salvage idea: force-schedule single-GPU pods onto mixed nodes by relaxing scheduler predicate `require_contiguous_mig=true` for low-risk pods. Danger: might cause OOMs if a pod actually needs contiguous slices mid-run. Should be emergency-only.

anika: we have an experimental toggle `scheduler.allow_mixed_placement` that will let binpacker place single-slice pods across mixed nodes but it disables pre-checks. Only enable if we see queue rising again.

oncall-ml: agreed. Hold override. Continue with routing + throttles + staged drains. Monitor closely.

ops-bot: infra-bot: starting first drain wave in 10m targeting 2 nodes. Cordon + drain will reduce pool capacity by ~1.8% temporarily.

luis: logging the incident ticket and interim status: INC-4809. I'm taking post-incident writeup.

rachel: note for follow-up: build node image init step that enforces MIG sizing at boot (or reconfigures FGs to consistent profiles). Add compatibility check in node pool upgrade pipeline so future rollouts don't mix profiles.

oncall-ml: handing off: I'll stay on for next 40m and then hand over to next oncall if stable. Action items: 1) monitor queue & 429s 2) confirm drains complete without OOMs 3) ensure router fallback remains healthy 4) infra to add MIG-init step 5) CS follow-up comms.

anika: starting drain waves now, staggered. Will post updates every 15m or on major changes.

ops-bot: INCIDENT state -> mitigated (P0 watch). Next scheduled update in 15m. :warning:
